title: Four seasons, one steppe
goal: Talking about weather, seasons and nature — a topic that in Mongolia isn't small talk but a matter of daily life.
bekal: describe the weather and the seasons accurately
use the *-ж байна* form for things happening in nature right now
understand why Mongolians always talk about the weather first

dialogs.title: Яриа — Аль улирал хамгийн сайхан вэ?
dialogs.intro: Early October. The first snow fell overnight. Budi and Sarnai are walking to campus.

lines.speaker: Буди:
lines.id: Sarnai, it's snowing! This is my first snow.
lines.literal: Sarnai O, snow enter-ing is! this my first's snow.

lines.speaker: Сарнай:
lines.id: Really? It never snows in Indonesia?
lines.literal: really Q? Indonesia-in snow enter-usually-not thing Q?

lines.speaker: Буди:
lines.id: Never. We have two seasons: rainy and not rainy.

lines.speaker: Сарнай:
lines.id: Only two? We have four, and all four are completely different.
lines.literal: two-only Q? us-to four be-usually, also all-four sharply different.

lines.speaker: Сарнай:
lines.id: Summer. The steppe is green and the herders move camp. Naadam is in summer too.

lines.speaker: Сарнай:
lines.id: Harsh. It can reach minus forty degrees. Sometimes there's a dzud.

lines.speaker: Сарнай:
lines.id: Heavy snow falls and the livestock can't find grass. Lots of animals die.

lines.speaker: Буди:
lines.id: That's terrible. What season is it now?

lines.speaker: Сарнай:

lines.speaker: Сарнай:
lines.id: Almost. Get your jacket ready, my boy!

notes: ⚠️ **Цас орж байна literally means "snow is entering".** Mongolian uses the verb *орох* (to enter) for snow and rain: *бороо орж байна* (it's raining), *цас орсон* (it snowed). English says snow "falls", Mongolian says it "enters" — both are images, and both make sense.

**Улирал = season, and Mongolia really has four sharply different ones.** The difference goes far beyond weather — it shapes all of life: when herders move camp, when Naadam is held, when schools break.

**Зуд has no equivalent in any other language.** It's a uniquely Mongolian disaster: a winter so harsh that livestock can't reach the grass under the snow or ice, and starve by the millions. ⚠️ The word entered English as *dzud* without translation, because there's no other word for it.

**Мал = livestock, and it's one of the most important words in Mongolian.** *Таван хошуу мал* ("five snouts of livestock") is the name for the five animals that sustain Mongolian life: horse, cow/yak, camel, sheep, goat. Mongolia has about seventy million head of livestock — twenty times its human population.
**The -аад / -ээд suffix means "after" and links two events.** *Цас ор**оод*** = "after the snow falls". It's the most common sentence linker in Mongolian, and it's covered fully at A2.

grammars.title: Talking about the weather
body: Two patterns cover almost everything you need to say: **adjective + байна** for a state, and **noun + -тай** for something that comes with the day.
after: ⚠️ Notice that weather sentences **have no subject at all**. *Хүйтэн байна* is literally just "cold is" — no "it", no "today". English has to add a dummy *it*; Mongolian doesn't bother. **One less word for you to worry about.**
**The standard question: *Цаг агаар ямар байна вэ?*** (What's the weather like?) or, shorter, *Гадаа ямар байна?* (How is it outside?).

grammars.title: The four seasons and what happens in them
body: The months don't fall in Mongolia quite as they do elsewhere, and each season has its own activities that set the calendar for the whole country.

head: Улирал
Say it
English
Months
What happens
rows: Dust storms; young animals are born; the hardest season.
Green steppe; Naadam; gers are moved.
Very short; getting ready for winter.

after: ⚠️ **Spring is the hardest season in Mongolia, not winter.** It's surprising but makes sense: the animals are thin after four months of cold, the grass hasn't grown yet, and dust storms blow in from the Gobi. When Mongolians say *хавар хэцүү*, they aren't complaining about the weather but about hunger.

**Наадам (NAA-dam) is the national festival on July 11–13**, with three events: wrestling (*бөх*), horse racing (*морин уралдаан*) and archery (*сурын харваа*). The name means "games", and it has been held since the time of Genghis Khan.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Тэнгэр means "sky" and also "God" in pre-Buddhist Mongolian belief.** *Мөнх тэнгэр* — "Eternal Heaven" — is the supreme power Genghis Khan named as the source of his mandate. To this day, Mongolians say *тэнгэр мэдэх* ("heaven knows") for things beyond human control, just like "God knows" or "heaven knows" in English.

blocks.title: Нутаг: a word you can't translate
items: *Нутаг* means land, territory **and home region** all at once — the place you were born and where your ancestors are buried.
*Нутаг руугаа явна* = "go back home to one's region", and every Mongolian has a *нутаг*, even after three generations in the city.
⚠️ The idea is close to "hometown" or "the old country" in English — a place that's more than just an address. **If you want a Mongolian to feel close to you right away, ask *Танай нутаг хаана вэ?***
*Нутгийн хүн* = someone from the same home region. This bond is very strong and often decides lifelong friendships.

sections.title: Talking about the weather in sentences

head: Sentence
Meaning
rows: It's really cold outside, you can't go out.
In spring the wind is strong.

blocks.text: In Mongolia, **talking about the weather isn't small talk the way it is in Britain — it's information people genuinely need.** The temperature can swing twenty degrees in a day, storms can come without warning, and roads can close. If someone asks you about the weather, answer seriously and add what you've seen.

head: Монгол
Say it
English
Why it matters
rows: Milk, meat, hide. Yaks for the highlands.
The main meat, wool for gers.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **These five animals are called *таван хошуу мал* — "the five snouts of livestock" — and their order isn't random.** The horse comes first because it made the Mongol Empire possible. The goat comes last because, though most profitable today, it damages the steppe by pulling grass up by the roots. The tension between cashmere money and protecting the steppe is one of the biggest debates in Mongolia today.

blocks.title: Sentences that make Mongolians smile
items: *Монголын байгаль үнэхээр сайхан.* — Mongolia's nature is truly beautiful.
*Би тал нутгийг үзмээр байна.* — I want to see the steppe.
*Гэрт хононд болох уу?* — May I stay the night in a ger?
*Морь унаж сурмаар байна.* — I want to learn to ride a horse.
